chunks: 5077 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Al-'Ala' and Abu Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام:

Regarding a man who said to his wife, “O adulteress, I committed adultery with you,” he عليه السلام said: “One legal punishment is upon him for his accusing her. As for his saying, ‘I committed adultery with you,’ there is no legal punishment upon him in that unless he testifies against himself four times to zina before the Imam.”

key_terms.زَنَيْتُ بِكِ: A claim by the speaker that he committed zina with her.
key_terms.عِنْدَ الْإِمَامِ: Before the Imam, i.e., the lawful judicial authority.
key_terms.لِقَذْفِهِ: For his slanderous accusation of adultery.
key_terms.يَا زَانِيَةُ: An accusation of adultery directed at the wife.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man says to his wife, 'O adulteress, I committed adultery with you'?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning qadhf and self-incrimination in a case involving a husband and wife. The accusation against the wife incurs the hadd for slanderous accusation, while the man's statement about himself does not establish the hadd of zina unless he confesses before the Imam four times.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5077 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Al-Ala and Abu Ayyub from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Jafar Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) regarding a man who said to his wife, "O' adulteress, I have committed adultery with you,"

Imam (as) said: "He is liable for one legal punishment for accusing her. As for his statement, 'I have committed adultery with you,' there is no legal punishment for that unless he testifies against himself four times for committing adultery before the Imam."
